# New renderings — iliad-083 (13.560–659)

| ἀμενηνόω (ἀμενήνωσεν … αἰχμήν, 13.562) | "made powerless" | "made … powerless" | "weakened", "blunted", "unnerved"; ἀμενηνός keeps the shipped "powerless" (iliad-035, 5.885) |

| σκῶλος πυρίκαυστος (13.564; σκῶλος rare, "stake" the usual guess) | "fire-burnt stake" | "a stake burnt in the fire" (+ note: exact sense of σκῶλος not certain) | "charred stake", "fire-hardened post" (each decides the unknown), "splinter" |
| αἰδοῖα (αἰδοίων, 13.568) | "the genitals" | "the genitals" | "the privates", "the groin", "the loins" (each moves the place); αἰδοῖος "revered" in the table is the same stem, noted in the unit |

| μετασπόμενος (13.567; ἕπομαι with μετά) | "following after" | "following after" | "pursuing", "chasing" (kept for διώκω); ἑσπόμενος (13.570) is "following" |

Departures from shared English: none. The lines of this part that stand in a published part take the published wording: 13.566, 13.596 and 13.648 (ἂψ δ’ ἑτάρων εἰς ἔθνος ἐχάζετο κῆρ’ ἀλεείνων, as in 3.32), 13.604 and 13.605 (as in 3.15 and 11.232, with "the son of Atreus" now Menelaus), 13.610 (as in 3.361) and 13.637 (the Odyssey’s 23.145, "sweet song-and-dance and blameless dancing"). 13.580 takes the shipped 5.659 wording, and 13.575 the table’s "and darkness covered his two eyes". The word "pulled out" and the whole simile at 13.571–575 are new (ἀσπαίρω keeps the table’s "gasping").
